draft.title: The endocrine system
card: The endocrine system is made of glands, such as the pancreas and thyroid. Glands release hormones, which are chemical messengers.
Hormones are released straight into the blood. The blood carries them around the body.
A hormone acts only on target cells. These cells have receptors that match the shape of that hormone.
Cells without the matching receptor do not respond to the hormone, even though the blood carries it past them.
draft.remember: Glands release hormones into the blood, and only cells with matching receptors respond.

a.q: Why do only some cells in the body respond to a particular hormone?
opts: Only those cells have receptors that match the hormone
Only those cells are reached by blood carrying the hormone
The gland sends the hormone directly to those cells
Only those cells are close to the gland
a.why: A hormone reaches most of the body in the blood, but only target cells have matching receptors. Blood passing a cell is not enough to cause a response.
a.clue: Think about what the hormone must attach to.

b.q: Sam has a drug that blocks the receptors for a hormone on liver cells only. Blood levels of the hormone stay normal. What is the likely result?
opts: Liver cells do not respond, but other target cells still do
All cells stop responding to the hormone
The gland stops releasing the hormone into the blood
Other cells with different receptors respond instead
b.why: Without working receptors, the liver cells cannot respond, even though the hormone is in the blood. Other target cells still have their receptors, so they respond as usual.

a.best: Only those cells have receptors that match the hormone

b.best: Liver cells do not respond, but other target cells still do
